 Learn more Goldman Sachs Group has delivered a powerful share price run over the past few years, and recent swings now put a sharper spotlight on whether that level still lines up with the returns it earns on its capital. With the stock giving back some ground in recent weeks, investors are asking if the current valuation fairly reflects the engine of profitability inside the franchise. 
 Over the past 3 years the stock has gained 222.9%, which puts a lot of weight on the question of whether the underlying return on capital profile is strong enough to support that kind of rerating. 
 Recent headlines around a revival in Goldman Sachs' advisory and investment banking activity, together with record wealth management assets and growing involvement in areas like AI financing and tokenization, can influence how durable investors expect fee income and capital returns to be over the long haul. 
 If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See what Goldman Sachs Group's 12.5x P/E says about the price . 
 For investors, the debate is whether the returns Goldman Sachs earns on the capital entrusted to it are sufficient to justify where the share price now sits. 
 If you want to test the same question you are asking about Goldman Sachs Group across a wider set of banks and capital markets businesses tied to AI and digital infrastructure, scan the 55 AI infrastructure stocks . 
 Is Goldman Sachs Group Still Cheap on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model starts with what Goldman Sachs earns on its equity relative to the return investors demand. On this view, each share is anchored by a book value of $372.25 and a stable book value estimate of $413.66, while stable EPS is set at $78.42 per share based on forecasts from 14 analysts. The cost of equity is $38.48 per share, which leaves an excess return of $39.93 per share and implies an average return on equity of 18.96% in the assumptions that feed the model. 
 Those inputs, together with a separate dividend stream where recent analysis puts dividend value at $370.80 per share and assumes 3.7% long run growth, feed into a view that the intrinsic worth of Goldman Sachs sits meaningfully above the current share price of $875.68. Because Q3 2026 results showed strong revenue and earnings alongside record wealth management inflows, the market reaction helps explain why the Excess Returns output still indicates more value than the current quotation embeds. Find out what Goldman Sachs Group could be worth using our Excess Returns estimate . 
 The Goldman Sachs Group Narrative: What Would Justify Today's Price? 
 Story Continues Narratives for Goldman Sachs Group pick up where the valuation puzzle leaves off and spell out which future paths for growth, margins and earnings would need to play out for the stock to be worth materially more or less than it trades at today on Simply Wall St's Community page. Instead of a single fair value figure, these scenarios unpack the future conditions that number relies on so you can monitor over time whether reality is tracking the story. 
 Community views on Goldman Sachs Group are split between a richer upside in fee and AI execution and a tighter focus on credit costs and balance sheet limits. 
 Bull case: 16% undervalued 
 "Firmwide technology and AI investment, reflected in lower headcount even as revenues grow and in management commentary on AI and process reengineering increasing productivity, supports the earlier view that automation and cloud can create operating leverage..."

 Bear case: 10% overvalued 
 "The numbers imply the share price already reflects Goldman Sachs Group delivering around high-teens to low-20s returns on equity with a growing mix of fee-based and financing income..."
